approach: Root cause: reading acceptance (`refusing_check`, crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs:520-551) is an ordered list of 13 `step!` checks, and none compares the request's explicit parts with the reading's deliverables and criteria. No rule says an explicit part stays in scope unless the request defers it. A reading that moves part (3) to `out_of_scope` or a follow-up is therefore accepted (jobs 20261029-084645-sza7 and 20261029-110953-bw7k). Fix it at that gate. (1) topics.rs gains a request-parts parser, `request_parts(text)`, beside `request_text_acceptance` and `is_bullet`, which stay unchanged. (2) checks.rs gains `pub fn check_request_parts(reading, request) -> Result<()>` and one `step!(check_request_parts(reading, request));` line placed LAST in `refusing_check`, so every existing refusal keeps its refusing check. (3) The check refuses a part that no criterion or deliverable path covers, including a part named only in `out_of_scope` or in a criterion that itself defers, unless the part's own text defers it. (4) Tests are in reading.rs and the corpus. (5) A CHANGELOG entry. Enforced by code; no prompt is edited. Revision: only the finding on criterion 8 is addressed; criterion 8 now states what fails without the behavior.

decisions.choice: Add a new parser `request_parts` in topics.rs and leave `request_text_acceptance`/`is_bullet` unchanged.
decisions.reason: `request_text_acceptance` is the parse `athena plan` uses (topics.rs:276, plan_entry at 411) and is also called by steward.rs:587/1566/1582/1658, hestia.rs:1781 and code_health.rs:1348. Changing it would move plan acceptance for queued requests. The corpus pins its bullet counts (`bullets_expected`, refusal_corpus.rs:2788-2794), and two cases pin 0 for `N)` and `(a)` parts as a known gap (refusal_corpus.rs:1891-1918).

rejected.why: It changes the plan acceptance of every queued request and the bullet counts the corpus pins; it is wider than the cause.

decisions.choice: Place the step last in `refusing_check`, after `check_reading_references`.
decisions.reason: Every existing refusal case keeps the check that refuses it, because the new step runs only when all others pass. `an_extra_check_with_no_case_is_reported` anchors on the `check_reading_references` step line (refusal_corpus.rs:2927) and still works. Only Accept cases with explicit parts can change.

rejected.why: It would pre-empt refusals such as `check_outcome_state` in the delivery cases that carry `2)` and `(a)` parts (refusal_corpus.rs:936-949), and change the refusing check of existing cases.

decisions.choice: Count explicit enumerated parts anywhere, and `-`/`*` bullets only after an `Acceptance:` line.
decisions.reason: The failure class is a dropped enumerated part such as (3). Acceptance bullets are the second introspection's proposal. Many existing tests run the real gate with short dash-bullet requests and scripted readings (reading.rs:2638, 2753, 2951; drain.rs:3988, 4067, 6320; job_plan.rs:166), and a free-form dash bullet is not a named part.

rejected.option: Treat every dash or star bullet as a part.
rejected.why: Larger blast radius over fixtures this planner cannot run, and a false-refusal risk on bullets a reader legitimately rewords.
It leaves out the request acceptance bullets that criterion 3 and introspection 20261029-111141-1661 name.

decisions.choice: Coverage means shared stems (at least min(2, n)) with one criterion that does not itself defer, or with one deliverable path; `out_of_scope` never covers. A part defers itself when its own text has a whole-word `DEFER_PHRASES` hit.
decisions.reason: This is the brief's match rule and gives 'drops or narrows' a testable form: a part reduced to a vague line shares too few stems. A part moved to `out_of_scope` is refused, which is the sza7 shape. The request's own deferral exempts the part, per criterion 4.

rejected.option: Require a deliverable and a criterion for every part.
rejected.why: A docs or study part may be met by a criterion alone, and deliverable paths rarely carry the words of a part; it would refuse good readings.

rejected.option: Count shared words across the whole reading text.
rejected.why: Summary and title echo the request, so a dropped part would still look covered.

decisions.choice: Enforce by code only; edit no prompt.
decisions.reason: The reader prompt budget is 1998 of 2000 (docs/system-facts.md budget line). The refusal text reaches the reader on its one corrected re-read (`read_for` passes the refusal back, reading.rs:720-759).

rejected.option: Add a rule line to the reader prompt.
rejected.why: There is no token headroom, and prose is not a mechanism.

risks.risk: False refusals of good readings, because a reader rewords a part so it shares fewer than min(2, n) stems with any criterion.
risks.mitigation: Parts with no significant stems are skipped; short generic gate bullets (fmt, clippy, test pass) have none. The threshold is 2 shared stems with a 6-character stem cut. The error names the part and the repair, and the reader gets one corrected re-read (reading.rs:738-759). The 10% share is declared as an estimate; Athena's replay of past readings measures it at verification, and the planner cannot run it because `records/` is absent.

risks.risk: An existing test with a scripted reading and a request that has an `Acceptance:` line or enumerated markers is newly refused, forcing edits outside the five listed deliverables (reading.rs:7396, 7743; run/tests.rs; drain.rs).
risks.mitigation: Dash bullets count only after an `Acceptance:` line, and the search found no enumerated markers in requests outside the corpus. The producer runs `cargo test --locked` before finishing and repairs the scripted reading's criteria, never the check, naming any such file in the report.

risks.risk: A marker list in prose, such as this request's 'such as (1), (2) and (3)', is read as parts, and its trailing sentence as part 3.
risks.mitigation: An inline sequence counts only when every marker has text with a significant word, and the last part ends at the first sentence end. Corpus case `request-parts-marker-list-without-text` pins this.

risks.risk: A deferral word in a part (`later`, `future`) is inside another word, or the reader writes 'follow-up' in a covering criterion to hide a drop.
risks.mitigation: `has_phrase` matches whole words (surveys.rs:39; 'latest' does not match, with a unit test). A criterion that itself defers does not cover a part, and corpus case `request-parts-covering-criterion-says-follow-up` refuses it.

risks.risk: The recorded request text of jobs sza7 and bw7k is not available to the planner, so the corpus shapes are rebuilt from the introspections' account.
risks.mitigation: The case `source` strings say 'rebuilt from the introspection's account', not 'verbatim'. The test of criterion 2 holds the property for any part (3), not for one job.

risks.risk: A stem cut to 6 characters can match unrelated words, so a dropped part is judged covered.
risks.mitigation: Coverage needs 2 shared stems in a single criterion or path. This is a known limit stated in the doc comment (a part whose words are all generic can be missed); it is a heuristic like the sibling checks.
